title: Dranyen (long-neck lute)
summary: The dranyen is a long-necked lute of the Himalayan highlands. A small round body covered with skin carries six strings in three pairs, and the neck ends in a carved dragon head. It is strummed and plucked to accompany songs and circle dances.
howToPlay: Three pairs of strings run up a neck with no frets; each lane marks where a note is played.
A bead slides down the string toward its place. Pluck the lane just as the bead lands.
Try the dance song in two groups of three first, then the circle dance, then call and answer.
Each tune is played through twice.
rules: The notes come from a five-note scale: D, E, F sharp, A and B, over two octaves.
The dance song is counted in two groups of three.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra plucks cost points.
Every tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: The dranyen is played at gatherings and festivals across the Himalayan highlands, where its ringing pairs of strings sit under sung verses and line dances. Makers still carve the neck and stretch the skin by hand.
credits: Tradition: the Himalayan dranyen; tunes written for this game
